articles.title: "If he were younger....": Sophie Cunningham’s shocking “dream man” confession has WNBA fans doing a double take
articles.summary: International Sports News: Sophie Cunningham has offered fans a glimpse into her dating preferences, and her answer was hardly the usual choice for a WNBA star. During a recent .
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham has offered fans a glimpse into her dating preferences, and her answer was hardly the usual choice for a WNBA star. During a recent podcast appearance, the Indiana Fever player named country music icon Alan Jackson when discussing her idea of a dream partner. Her playful confession quickly became a talking point because Jackson is much older than Cunningham and has been married for decades.Sophie Cunningham names Alan Jackson as her dream manCunningham discussed relationships and music during an appearance on the Like a Farmer podcast. The conversation took an unexpected turn when Alan Jackson's name came up.The 30-year-old basketball player made it clear that she has a soft spot for the country singer, who is 67. Rather than simply naming him as a celebrity she admires, Cunningham added a few conditions that would need to change before he could fit her idea of an ideal partner.'"I know I'm missing out on so much... Alan Jackson", she said.'The comment was clearly delivered with humor, but it still caught attention because of the age gap and Jackson's well-known personal life.Cunningham then elaborated on her unusual celebrity crush.“My God, Alan Jackson. If he were younger, weren't married and had children... he's everyone's dream guy.”Her remarks quickly turned the conversation into something more than a discussion about country music. Jackson has been married to Denise Jackson since 1979, and the couple have remained a familiar presence throughout his long career. That makes Cunningham's hypothetical scenario just that, a playful fantasy rather than an actual romance prospect.Still, the choice says something about Cunningham's personal taste. Instead of picking a younger athlete or a celebrity closer to her own age, she singled out one of country music's most established stars.Sophie Cunningham explains what she wants in a relationshipCunningham's comments did not stop with Alan Jackson. She also offered a few clues about what she would want from a relationship.One surprising detail involved height. Cunningham said she would not rule out dating a man who was shorter than her. In fact, she suggested that being taller could give her a particular feeling within the relationship.She joked that dating a shorter man could make her feel like " she is the man" in the relationship.At the same time, Cunningham said she would want her partner to lead the household. That combination makes her preferences less straightforward than a simple list of physical traits. She appeared more interested in the dynamic between two people and the roles they might naturally take on.Her comments also fit with the relaxed personality fans have seen from Cunningham away from the court. The WNBA player has frequently attracted attention for her humor and willingness to share candid moments online.Her connection to country music also has a personal angle. Cunningham's time in Missouri helped deepen her appreciation for the genre, making her admiration for Jackson less random than it might initially seem.For now, there is no romance story behind the comments. Jackson remains married to Denise, while Cunningham's remarks remain a humorous look at her celebrity preferences.But that did not stop fans from having fun with her answer. In a sports world often dominated by statistics, trades and game results, Cunningham's unexpected confession offered something very different: a lighthearted look at the person behind the WNBA uniform.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo listed his 23-acre Cheshire estate with a 7-bedroom mansion for $7.4 million; after more than 18 months on the market, it fell to $6.7 million
articles.summary: International Sports News: Cristiano Ronaldo’s former Cheshire estate was listed for about $7.4 million in 2023, but the asking price was later reduced to around $6.7 million af.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo’s former Cheshire estate was listed for about $7.4 million in 2023, but the asking price was later reduced to around $6.7 million after the property struggled to find a buyer. The huge estate in Alderley Edge covers 23 acres and includes a seven-bedroom mansion, six bathrooms, an indoor heated pool, gym, sauna, jacuzzi and cinema. There are also tennis and padel courts and a separate two-bedroom guest barn. Ronaldo moved into the property after returning to Manchester United in 2021, but his family soon moved to another Cheshire home. The estate was later put up for sale after his move to Saudi Arabia.What does Cristiano Ronaldo’s 23-acre Cheshire estate includeRonaldo’s former Cheshire home is built on a scale that goes well beyond a typical luxury house. The estate covers 23 acres in Alderley Edge, one of the well-known wealthy areas in Cheshire, while the main mansion has seven bedrooms and six bathrooms.The house was designed with both family life and fitness in mind. The main bedroom has private dressing areas and walk-in wardrobe space, while the other bedrooms have en-suite facilities.A large leisure area is one of the biggest features of the property. It has an indoor heated swimming pool, sauna and jacuzzi, along with a professional gym. For entertainment, there is a private cinema room and a wine cellar.The outdoor space adds even more to the property. Ronaldo’s former estate has a full-sized tennis court and a padel court, giving the owner options for sport without leaving the grounds.There is also a separate two-bedroom guest barn. It provides additional space for visitors, staff or security personnel while keeping the main house private.When Jackson-Stops listed the property, the estate agency described it as a “masterpiece of modern design set in 23 acres - an ultra stylish main residence with superb leisure suite, two bedroom guest barn and padel court.”Why did Cristiano Ronaldo leave the Cheshire mansion after returning to Manchester UnitedRonaldo did not stay in the mansion for long after returning to Manchester United in 2021. He and his family moved out soon after arriving in the area and shifted to another property in Cheshire.One explanation that appeared in reports at the time involved the land around the house. The estate bordered open farmland, and early-morning noise from sheep was said to have been a problem for Ronaldo.However, that detail has been disputed and should not be treated as the confirmed reason for the move. Privacy and security were also reported as concerns, especially because a public footpath ran close to the property.For someone as well known as Ronaldo, having people regularly passing near the estate could make privacy harder to maintain. His family therefore moved to another Cheshire property that had previously been owned by former Manchester United striker Andrew Cole.That home offered stronger security measures, including electric gates and CCTV, making it a better fit for the family.Why was Cristiano Ronaldo’s Cheshire estate listed for sale in 2023Ronaldo’s second Manchester United spell ended in November 2022 after his contract was terminated by mutual consent. The decision followed his high-profile television interview with Piers Morgan, in which he openly criticized the club and its leadership.A few weeks later, Ronaldo began the next stage of his career in Saudi Arabia after signing for Al-Nassr. That move also changed where he and his family spent most of their time.With Ronaldo no longer playing in Manchester, keeping a 23-acre estate in Cheshire made less sense. The property had already not been his family’s main home during the latter part of his United spell.Jackson-Stops placed the estate on the market in February 2023 with an asking price of £5.5 million, which was about $7.4 million based on the conversion used for the listing.The sale came as Ronaldo’s property holdings continued to stretch across several countries. Rather than keeping a large home in northern England that he was no longer using, the Cheshire estate became a property he could sell.Why did Cristiano Ronaldo’s property price fall to $6.7 millionFinding a buyer for a property of this size can take time. Ronaldo’s Cheshire estate remained on the market for more than 18 months, and the asking price was eventually reduced by £500,000.The new guide price was £5 million, or about $6.7 million.The reduction does not mean the property was sold for $6.7 million. It was the lower asking price after the original listing failed to attract a buyer within the expected period.There are practical reasons why a property like this can take longer to sell. The estate has 23 acres of land, which means a buyer is taking on much more than the upkeep of a normal house. The mansion also has a long list of specialist facilities, including an indoor pool, gym, tennis court and padel court.Those features can be attractive to the right buyer, but they can also make the property more expensive and demanding to maintain.The price cut also stands out because Ronaldo has previously experienced a difficult sale in the same area.How did Cristiano Ronaldo’s earlier Cheshire home perform when he sold itRonaldo owned another house in Alderley Edge during his first Manchester United spell. That property was a five-bedroom brick house with luxury facilities, including an indoor swimming pool and gym.He bought the earlier property in 2008 for a reported £3.895 million. It was eventually sold in 2019 for £3.25 million, meaning the sale price was around £645,000 lower than what he had originally paid.That house and the current 23-acre estate are different properties, but both show that even a famous footballer’s luxury home can take time to sell.The current estate was bought around Ronaldo’s return to Manchester United and later became unnecessary after his career moved away from England. Its large size and unusual collection of facilities also put it into a small section of the property market.For now, the important change is the asking price. Ronaldo’s former seven-bedroom Cheshire estate went from about $7.4 million to $6.7 million, but a final sale price has not been confirmed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "I’m too scared": Angel Reese makes a bold promise about her love life and fans may have to wait for a ring
articles.summary: International Sports News: Angel Reese has drawn a firm line between her public career and her private life. The Chicago Sky star has made it clear that fans should not expect r.
articles.body: Angel Reese has drawn a firm line between her public career and her private life. The Chicago Sky star has made it clear that fans should not expect regular relationship updates from her social media accounts. Reese explained that the intense attention surrounding her dating life changed the way she views romance in the public eye, leading her to make one striking promise about what she will share next.Angel Reese explains why her dating life stays privateReese opened up about her approach to relationships during an episode of her podcast Unapologetically Angel in 2024. At the time, she was speaking with stylist Law Roach when the conversation turned toward dating and the pressure that can come with being a highly visible athlete.The topic was especially relevant for Reese. At 6-foot-4, she is already one of the most recognizable players in the WNBA, and her life away from basketball often attracts almost as much attention as what happens on the court.She admitted that she was unsure whether she would date someone shorter than her, even though she did not completely rule it out.“I don’t know. I’m too scared,” Reese said when discussing the possibility.But her biggest message was not about height. It was about privacy.Reese had previously addressed the issue on social media after her dating life became a subject of intense online discussion. Her frustration was clear.“Now i see why people hide relationships & keep everything private 😭 like i don’t think i’ll ever openly share that part of my life with yall again until im married cause yall do THE MOST!”The post reflected a growing divide between what Reese was willing to share with fans and what she wanted to keep for herself. For someone whose professional life is constantly dissected, a private relationship offered a rare space where she could simply be Angel rather than an athlete under a microscope.Angel Reese makes one promise about her next relationship postReese later made her position even clearer during another episode of Unapologetically Angel, this time while speaking with Pretty Vee.“I think the next time I’ll post I’m in a relationship [on social media] is when I’m married,” Bayou Barbie said. “And that’s some time from now, so you ain’t gonna see it.”She followed that statement with another playful warning for anyone hoping to catch a glimpse of her dating life.“You might see me on a date. You gonna have to catch me though,” she continued. “Like, I’m not gonna post a man on my page.”A few days later, Reese reinforced the message herself.“The next time I’ll post in a relationship is when I’m married,” Reese wrote.Her stance makes sense in an era when a single photo can trigger days of speculation. For high-profile athletes, dating rumors can quickly become headlines, fan debates and social media arguments. Reese has experienced that attention firsthand, so choosing not to feed it gives her greater control over her personal life.Ironically, her relationship with Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. later became widely known despite her earlier promise. Rumors about the pair began circulating in early 2025, before Carter appeared at Reese’s birthday celebration and supported her courtside later that year.That does not necessarily erase the point Reese was making. Her comments were about refusing to turn a relationship into regular social media content.Reese's career has only made that boundary more important. As a first overall pick, three-time All-Star and one of the WNBA's most closely followed young stars, she knows almost every part of her life can become public conversation.Her solution is refreshingly direct. Fans can watch her compete, follow her career and celebrate her achievements. Her romantic life, however, does not have to become another performance.And if Reese stays true to the promise she made, the next relationship announcement may come with a very different title attached to it: husband.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Gukesh not in a position to defend anything': Magnus Carlsen on World Chess Championship clash vs Javokhir Sindarov
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: Five-time world champion Magnus Carlsen has pushed back against the framing of D Gukesh's upcoming World Championship match as a \"title def.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Five-time world champion Magnus Carlsen has pushed back against the framing of D Gukesh's upcoming World Championship match as a "title defence", arguing that the Indian should instead be approaching it as an opportunity to gain rather than something to protect.Speaking to the reporters on the sidelines of the Global Chess League (GCL) on Thursday, Carlsen said the way Gukesh has played over the past two years means he shouldn't see himself as merely holding onto what he already has."The word 'defend' is really not a good place to begin, because in terms of how Gukesh has played for the last couple of years, he should not be in a position where he has to defend anything," Carlsen said. "He should be in a position where he has everything to gain."The Norwegian pointed to Gukesh's 2024 form as evidence of his ceiling."He has shown previously in 2024 that when things click, he has the potential to play at an extremely high level," Carlsen remarked, adding that while public confidence in a repeat performance may be low, that only sharpens the challenge in front of him. "I don't think a lot of people believe that he will do it now, but I think it's even more of an interesting challenge for him to try and get back to that."Carlsen was also blunt about the psychological dimension of the contest, suggesting the mental battle could prove just as decisive as anything on the board."Chess is a highly psychological game, so it probably won't take a lot to potentially place some doubts in Sindarov's mind and some confidence for Gukesh," he said.Asked whether Gukesh's current form would matter once the match got underway, Carlsen, who is currently playing for the APL Pipers in the fourth season of GCL, was candid about his broader scepticism of the classical World Championship format itself, calling it a poor mechanism for identifying the strongest player."One of the reasons why I believe it's an extraordinarily bad way to determine the best player in the world is that you play classical, which is the most egalitarian format, and you don't play a ton of games as well," he explained. Even a heavily lopsided pre-match assessment, he said, rarely translates into a lopsided scoreline."If you think a certain match is 80-20 before it starts, the likelihood is still very high that it's going to be a close score, because chess is such a drawish game."On the matchup itself, Carlsen was unequivocal that Gukesh holds his own against Sindarov in pure quality."Gukesh has shown that his ceiling is on par or better than Sindarov," he added. But given the short format, he warned that early momentum could decide everything."If Sindarov is ahead early on, it's probably very, very bad news for Gukesh. If Gukesh is ahead early on, he automatically becomes a significant favourite. That's how these matches work."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Spider-Man, Batman all had to pay rent: Magnus Carlsen, now a father, is no exception
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: Peter Parker still has to make rent. That's the part of the superhero myth that doesn't generally make it to the big screen.Spider-Man save.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Peter Parker still has to make rent. That's the part of the superhero myth that doesn't generally make it to the big screen.Spider-Man saves New York by night and shoots freelance photographs by day, not because he loves deadlines, but because somebody has to pay for groceries. Bruce Wayne funds the Batcave through a company he actually has to run. Even the billionaires among comic-book heroes tend to keep one foot planted in something as unglamorous as payroll, because the world they're protecting doesn't pause its bills just because they're busy saving it.The genius of that storytelling trope isn't the fighting. It's the quiet insistence that even extraordinary people don't get to opt out of ordinary responsibility. You can bend steel, but you still have to show up for the version of yourself that provides.It's a strange place to start a story about arguably the greatest chess player who has ever lived. But it's exactly where Magnus Carlsen's own words landed, almost a year into fatherhood, when this journalist asked him what had actually changed since his son was born during a media interaction on the sidelines of the Global Chess League (GCL)."In my professional life, things haven't changed that dramatically," he replied almost instantly. "I'm still the provider for the family, so I still work."Read that sentence twice. Here is a man who has spent two decades rewriting the ceiling of human chess ability, who has been declared unbeatable so many times that "unbeatable" started to feel like a job description rather than a compliment and the frame he reaches for, unprompted, to describe his life now is the oldest one in the book. Provider. Worker.The guy who still has to go to the office, except the office is a tournament hall on the other side of the world and the job is being the best that has ever done this.There's a reason that instinct runs so deep it shows up even in someone whose entire identity has otherwise been built on exceptionalism.Strip away the grandmaster titles and the rating numbers, and you're left with something Charles Darwin sketched out over a century and a half ago. In species where offspring depend heavily on parental care, one of the strongest pressures shaping behaviour is the survival and successful reproduction of the next generation.Natural selection doesn't reward talent, glory, or achievement for their own sake. It favours traits and behaviours that, on average, contribute to reproductive success. In a species where raising offspring is essential to that success, provisioning and protecting them can become an extraordinarily powerful behavioural priority.Every other instinct, ambition, or appetite can be renegotiated when that responsibility arrives. It's why the same species that produces reckless risk-takers also produces the most disciplined, repetitive, unglamorous labour imaginable, generation after generation, the instant there's a mouth to feed.Carlsen, without reaching for any of that language himself, described exactly this mechanism happening in real time inside his own life."Yeah, I love it (being a father)," he said, when asked how fatherhood had actually felt. "My son is the greatest human being alive. So, yeah, it's fantastic. It's a joy every day."Then, almost in the same breath, the other half of the equation. "It's a little bit sad to be away from him now, but I also have to provide for my family," he sighed.That sentence is the whole feature in miniature. Joy and duty, sitting right next to each other, unable to cancel each other out.It also explains something that had puzzled a lot of people watching Carlsen's career from the outside. Why would the greatest player alive walk away from the one title that carries his name to the widest audience, the classical World Championship, at the exact moment he could have kept collecting it?His own answer, delivered without a trace of nostalgia, sounded less like retirement and more like a man doing the math on his own limited hours."After I became a father as well, it made it even more certain for me that I was never coming back to the classical world championship," he told us, the reporters covering the GCL in Bengaluru.Not because he'd fallen out of love with chess.He was careful to draw that line clearly. "There are so many things that I like about chess. There are a lot of tournaments that I like. There are a lot of formats that I like," Magnus, currently plying his trade for defending champions APL Pipers, asserted.The classical world title specifically, though, had become something he "genuinely" disliked spending his finite time on, and once there was a small person at home whose future depended on how he spent his hours, "when there's no kind of competitive reason why I should, it makes zero sense."That's not the language of a man slowing down. It's the language of a man reallocating.Good enough, but when asked to reveal his son's name, the one detail every journalist in the room clearly wanted, Carlsen drew a boundary with the instinctive protectiveness of someone guarding something more fragile than a chess position."I can talk in general terms about my son. I think he's great, but I'm not sure I can do that," he said, gently declining. It's a small thing, a single guarded sentence in a room full of questions about tournaments and ratings. But it's also the most on-brand fatherhood answer imaginable.Somewhere between Darwin's finches and Peter Parker's rent money sits Magnus Carlsen, age 35, five-time world champion, currently building his entire professional calendar around a person the public isn't even allowed to know the name of. He didn't need evolutionary biology to explain why. He just needed one sentence. For him, it's a joy every day, and he still has to go to work because, you know, in a world where superheroes are not spared, not all superheroes wear capes.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: At the Asian Games in Japan, president of the Softball Association of India, Neetal Narang, will assume the responsibility of a safeguarding officer.An IOC and OCA-certified safeguarding officer, Neetal has undergone several certification courses conducted by the continental body over the past two years.“Safeguarding is not just about a few aspects like sexual harassment or bullying. We deal with a wider aspect of issues like physical, psychological and sexual abuse, harassment, neglect, discrimination and bullying. We tend to normalise or brush under the carpet issues like body shaming, which will also come under the safeguarding officer’s purview,” Neetal told TOI.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Need some luck”: George Russell breaks silence on Kimi Antonelli and reveals why his F1 title fight has become so tough
articles.summary: International Sports News: George Russell is refusing to pretend that the Formula 1 championship battle is closer than it looks. With Kimi Antonelli holding a 66-point advantage.
articles.body: George Russell is refusing to pretend that the Formula 1 championship battle is closer than it looks. With Kimi Antonelli holding a 66-point advantage, the Mercedes driver has admitted that his team mate has been the stronger performer so far this season. Russell still has his eyes on the title, but he knows the numbers are not in his favor. Antonelli arrives at the Spanish Grand Prix after another big win at Monza, while Russell is looking for a response. The Briton believes his recent form has improved, but he also accepts that something extra may be needed if he is to turn the championship around.George Russell gives Kimi Antonelli credit while refusing to walk away from the title fightThe gap between the two Mercedes drivers has become one of the biggest stories of the 2026 season. Russell made a strong start to the year, but Antonelli has gradually taken control of the championship with a remarkable run of results.The Italian has now won seven races, including a dramatic comeback at Monza after starting 19th. Russell finished second in Italy, but he could not prevent his team mate from taking another major step toward the title.Russell was direct when assessing the situation.“I'm not trying to be delusional, the reality is my team mate has done a better job than me this year. Had some bad luck but he deserves to be leading and right now he deserves to be in the position he is.“From my side, I'm just going race by race, going to try and win as many as possible. If I want to win this championship I'm going to need some luck and that's where we are. I'm being quite realistic about the position we're in.”That honesty does not mean Russell has given up. His focus is now on getting the most out of every race rather than worrying about the championship standings.He also praised Antonelli's consistency, pointing out that the 19-year-old has not suffered a bad weekend in terms of performance. That level of form has made Russell's task even harder.George Russell faces a fresh challenge at the new Madrid circuit with Kimi Antonelli aheadThe Spanish Grand Prix presents a different challenge because the Madring circuit in Madrid is new to Formula 1. Drivers have limited experience of the layout, meaning confidence and adaptability could play a major role.Russell believes the circuit will demand plenty from the drivers, particularly through its high-speed sections and aggressive kerbs.“The level of everyone in F1 is exceptionally high,” he said. “It’s going to be a circuit where you need confidence.“Very challenging, lots of high speed corners, aggressive kerbs. Going to be an experience for sure. Just try and keep out of the wall and build up to it.“Every race is an opportunity. This circuit is among the most risky circuits of the season. You want to put everything on the line and go for pole and victory but how I approach this race, it's just going about business as usual.”That mindset could be important for Russell. The championship deficit is significant, but there are still races remaining and opportunities to collect points.For now, Russell appears more interested in finding speed than calculating the title standings. Antonelli has the advantage, but the Mercedes driver knows the championship can change quickly in Formula 1.His task is clear. He needs to keep improving, win as many races as possible and hope the luck he has been missing this season eventually arrives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Annu Rani out of Asian Games squad; injury-returning Avinash Sable seals 3,000m steeplechase berth
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Hangzhou Asian Games gold medallist Annu Rani has lost her place in India’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games squad after failing to achieve the qua.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Hangzhou Asian Games gold medallist Annu Rani has lost her place in India’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games squad after failing to achieve the qualification standard in women’s javelin throw, TOI has reliably learnt.The development came after the Indian Athletics Final Series at the JLN stadium on Thursday, where Asian Games-bound athletes assessed their form, fitness and injury status, while seeking a final opportunity to attain the qualifying mark.Annu won gold with a 57.50m throw, but fell 12cm short of the 57.62m Games qualification standard. Sources informed the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) had made it clear to athletes before the event that the qualification benchmark had to be met.“Anyone who has not achieved the qualification standard will not be sent to the Asian Games. That was the AFI’s clear position. So, if Annu Rani has not qualified, she will not go. Those who have not achieved the mark will not be part of the contingent,” AFI planning committee chairman Lalit K Bhanot told TOI.In contrast, Avinash Sable delivered when it mattered most. Returning to his specialist 3,000m steeplechase after a 14-month injury-enforced hiatus, the 31-year-old clocked 8:32.39 to win gold and clear the 8:36.57 qualification standard.Sable, who underwent surgery for an ACL and meniscus injury after stumbling at the water jump during the last year’s Monaco Diamond League, is now set to defend his Asian Games steeplechase title.TOI has learnt that his entry in the men’s 5,000m has also been accepted by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) through the Games organisers, paving the way for a double-event appearance. “He will compete in both events. We discussed his participation in the 5,000m with the Games organisers, and that has been cleared,” Bhanot said. “If Sable had not qualified in the 3,000m steeplechase here, he would not have competed in the event either,” he added.Meanwhile, Hangzhou Games 100m hurdles silver medallist Jyothi Yarraji, CWG high-jump medallist Sarvesh Anil Kushare and triple jumper Praveen Chithravel have been asked to submit fitness certificates before travelling. All three are returning from injury and must establish fitness. Failure to produce the certificates could jeopardise their Games participation.At Thursday’s meet, hammer thrower Tanya Chaudhary set the lone national record, throwing the implement 68.35m. Ancy Sojan won the long jump with 6.76m, while Tajinderpal Singh Toor took shot-put gold with 20.64m.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Let me just play a little bit’: Geet Sethi makes billiards comeback at 65
articles.summary: More sports News: BENGALURU: He doesn’t look his age of 65, but Indian cuesports legend Geet Sethi is quick to acknowledge that appearances can be deceptive.“I may not .
articles.body: BENGALURU: He doesn’t look his age of 65, but Indian cuesports legend Geet Sethi is quick to acknowledge that appearances can be deceptive.“I may not look it, but I feel my age,” he laughs.But Sethi is like the classics — timeless. The ace cueist, who first picked up a cue in 1974, is set to return to competitive billiards next month, six years after his last appearance at the World Billiards Championship.The Ahmedabad-based player, who reached the knockouts in the 2018 edition, will return to the world stage in Great Wyrley, England, from Oct 19 to 22.Sethi’s comeback story began earlier this year when his peer and former cueist Ashok Shandilya coaxed him into playing a cuesports league in Dadar, Mumbai.“I played that tournament without really practising. But it was so much fun. Then I came back home and said to myself, ‘Let me start. Let me just play a little bit,’” Sethi told TOI.Another spark was lit at the Sports Club of Gujarat in June.“The tournament was on the same lines as what I played earlier in Mumbai. Again, it was so much fun playing with music in the background and getting to meet the entire fraternity,” said the cuesports exponent-turned-seasoned entrepreneur.“It was so good to meet everybody collectively for a long period of time. Since then, I’ve been playing every day. I began to play decently enough to kind of start enjoying the game again. So that’s where the whole trigger started from,” added the nine-time world billiards champion.Before that tournament, Sethi had largely kept in touch with the sport by playing snooker occasionally.But it was a fellow member of the Sports Club of Gujarat who eventually nudged him towards the world championship.“A club member kept pushing me. The thought really came when I started making breaks of 100 and 180. When you start enjoying the game, then the thought comes,” Sethi said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Eagles news: Sean Mannion justifies major Week 1 play-calling decision
articles.summary: Sean Mannion is taking a different view of the Philadelphia Eagles’ offense, quite literally. Ahead of Sunday’s 2026 season opener against the Washington Com...
articles.body:
Sean Mannion is taking a different view of the Philadelphia Eagles ' offense, quite literally. Ahead of Sunday's 2026 season opener against the Washington Commanders , Mannion confirmed he will call plays from the coaches' booth rather than the sideline. He explained that the elevated perspective gives him a cleaner view of defensive fronts, coverage rotations, and spacing across the field. This should allow him to process information without the distractions of sideline traffic. The vantage point should also help Mannion identify patterns between plays and communicate adjustments quickly to quarterback Jalen Hurts .

It is a significant choice for an offensive coordinator preparing for his first regular-season game calling an NFL offense. This is particularly true as Philadelphia introduces a revamped system. Sure, sideline play-callers can benefit from immediate interaction with players. However, Mannion believes seeing all 22 players develop from above will provide a clearer tactical picture. With Nick Sirianni handling the energy and operations on the field, the Eagles are establishing a coordinated command structure before their NFC East opener.

Philadelphia enters 2026 with Super Bowl aspirations and a roster full of established stars. Mannion's offense will center on Hurts and Saquon Barkley . DeVonta Smith will be the focal point of the receiving corps. The offensive line remains anchored by All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson . Defensively, the Eagles' unit features Jalen Carter up front alongside a promising secondary led by Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean . That combination gives the Eagles plenty of firepower on both sides of the ball. Now, Mannion's booth decision will face its first real examination. If his elevated perspective produces quicker reads and cleaner adjustments, Philadelphia may have found an important advantage before the season has even properly begun.

articles.title: Cowboys agree to terms with WR Ryan Flournoy on one-year extension
articles.summary: The Cowboys have agreed to terms with wide receiver Ryan Flournoy on a one-year contract extension, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.
articles.body:
The Cowboys have agreed to terms with wide receiver Ryan Flournoy on a one-year contract extension, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.

Flournoy, 26, was entering the final year of his deal, which will pay him $1.075 million in 2026. He would have become a restricted free agent in 2027.

After being waived out of training camp, Flournoy became the team's third wide receiver last season. He caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns, earning a promotion to the active roster from the practice squad early in the season.

The Cowboys drafted him in the sixth round in 2024, and he played 156 offensive snaps and 140 on special teams in 11 games as a rookie.

The team's leading receiver from last season, George Pickens , is playing under the one-year franchise tag and is scheduled to become a free agent in March.

articles.title: Sioux Falls public schools gear up for Presidents Bowl
articles.summary: SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — Four faces, four schools and two games. Saturday’s Presidents Bowl between the Sioux falls public schools is sure to be a great da...
articles.body:
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — Four faces, four schools and two games. Saturday's Presidents Bowl between the Sioux falls public schools is sure to be a great day of football and ahead of kickoff each team took a moment to realize just how big these games are.

"It's the pageantry, it's the bands, it's all the student section. You know, it just, it feels like a big time event," Lincoln Head Coach Jared Fredenburg said.

The Presidents Bowl is one of the oldest bowl games in South Dakota, dating back 34 years to the first game in 1992.

Since then, it's grown to become one of the biggest events on the high school athletics calendar.

"I'm a guy that grew up in Sioux Falls. So I've been coming to this since I was born. It's always been a big deal," Roosevelt Defensive Coordinator Brandon Mohr said.

"There isn't any other stage like it in Sioux Falls football until the playoffs, really," Washington Head Coach Ryan Evans added.

With a stage so big for both players and coaches, Jefferson Head Coach Eric Struck says there is a balance between excitement and preparation.

"You try not to make it a bigger deal than what it is. You try not to get caught up in the moment, but at the same time, you only get so many of these opportunities, you know, you get one a week. So go out and enjoy it and make the most of it," Struck said.

In this year's edition of the bowl, Washington will battle Roosevelt at 2:00 p.m. while Jefferson will take on Lincoln in the second game at 5:00.

"I just want to see our kids go out and have fun and play and let loose and show that we're turning a corner at Roosevelt, it's a big opportunity for us," Mohr said.

"It's, you know, turning into a rivalry between Jefferson and Lincoln, two talented teams. So the kids are already excited. They're already fired up," Struck said.

With kickoff rapidly approaching, a pair of coaches talked about what excites them most about this weekend.

"Lincoln winning. That's what I'm looking forward to," Fredenburg said.

"Kickoff. I got, my blood, my blood just gets going. I get goosebumps and maybe that's the kid in me, but it's so exciting," Evans said.

We will have highlights of both Presidents Bowl games on KELOLAND news on Saturday.

articles.title: ‘Never seen so many errors’: Fans stunned as Elena Rybakina beats Coco Gauff to reach US Open final
articles.summary: Tennis fans have reacted strongly after Elena Rybakina came from a set down to beat Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 and reach her first US Open final. Rybakina, who...
articles.body:
Tennis fans have reacted strongly after Elena Rybakina came from a set down to beat Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 and reach her first US Open final.

Rybakina, who became world No. 1 just a day earlier, recovered after losing the opening set before breaking Gauff twice in the deciding set to seal the win.

The result sets up a huge final against Aryna Sabalenka, who defeated Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2 in the other semi-final. Sabalenka has won 20 consecutive matches at the US Open and leads Rybakina 10-7 in their head-to-head record.

Coco Gauff defeat sparks strong reaction from tennis fans

Gauff took control early, breaking Rybakina in the sixth game before serving out the opening set 6-3. However, Rybakina responded in the second, breaking for 3-1 and eventually forcing a deciding set.

The third set went back and forth before Rybakina finally created the decisive opening at 4-3. Gauff immediately broke back after Rybakina served for the match at 5-3, but the new world No. 1 responded again in the 10th game to complete the victory.

Fans were quick to focus on the number of errors during the contest, with one writing: "Never seen so many errors in one match"

Another supporter was critical of Gauff's recent form, posting: "Bad phase for Coco, has to gear up fast to stay relevant"

There was also plenty of praise for Rybakina, with one fan writing: "Congrats Elena! Cannot wait to see final- congrats on #1"

Another simply celebrated Gauff's defeat, saying: "Thank god, I thought Coco would never lose!"

One supporter compared Gauff's development to boxing heavyweight Deontay Wilder, writing:

"Coco needs a coach that will refine her skills instead of having her rely on pure athleticism. It's like Deontay Wilder in boxing."

Rybakina's level in the final two sets also drew praise ahead of the Sabalenka showdown:

"Sablenka can't beat Rybakina if Rybakina produce this much high level Technicall game like she did in 2&3 set."

Not everyone was convinced by Rybakina's performance, however: "Rybakina is the worst #1 I've ever seen: unforced errors galore, doesn't move well, doesn't volley well. Watching her play is infuriating."

And one final reaction summed up the excitement around the result: "Thank you. Tennis wins with this result. Proper tennis"

Rybakina will now face Sabalenka on Saturday with her first US Open title and another major milestone within reach.

articles.title: What Garcia and Benn each need to get right at T-Mobile Arena
articles.summary: Speed against power, a title run against a level jump. Here's what Garcia and Benn each have to get right at T-Mobile Arena.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — Ryan Garcia skipped Tuesday's scheduled face-off with Conor Benn, and when he was asked about it at Wednesday's media day, he didn't dress it up. He said he simply didn't want to be there, that he's skipped face-offs throughout his career, and that he'd never even heard of one happening on a Wednesday. He pointed out there are three more chances to stand across from Benn before Saturday, at Thursday's press conference, Friday's weigh-in, and the ring walk itself, and said he was just sticking to the routine he keeps during fight week. By Thursday, both fighters are in the same room for the final press conference, and the questions figure to get sharper.

The stakes are straightforward. Garcia defends the WBC welterweight title he won in February over Mario Barrios, his first defense in the same building he fights in again. Benn arrives 25-1 with 14 knockouts, unbeaten at welterweight since moving back down from 160 to beat Regis Prograis in his Zuffa Boxing debut this past April, the win that got him here. It's his first world title shot, and a chance to do in Las Vegas what his father, Nigel Benn, never quite managed.

What decides it comes down to what both guys do with their hands.

Garcia's path runs through his hand speed. Nobody at 147 turns speed into finishing power the way he does when he's set correctly, and that speed is what broke Barrios down over twelve rounds. The concern with Garcia has never been the ceiling. It's the floor. He's shown he can be hit clean and hurt by a fighter willing to sit down and trade, which is how he lost to Rolando Romero. Benn hits harder than Romero does. If Garcia treats the opening rounds like an audition instead of a fight, that's the window Benn is looking for.

Benn's path is about weight of shot and volume. He's spent two years proving he can take a firm chin and keep coming, first against Chris Eubank Jr. twice, then against Prograis. His hole is the level jump. Garcia hits with a different kind of speed than anyone Benn has faced at this weight, and Benn has never had to solve a problem that fast. If he tries to walk Garcia down in a straight line without cutting off the ring first, he spends the night chasing instead of landing.

On paper, the resume favors Garcia. He's shared a ring with names like Devin Haney and Romero at a higher volume of marquee fights than Benn has seen. Benn's two best wins, the Eubank rematch and Prograis, both came at a different weight than Saturday's. That doesn't make his resume thin. It makes Saturday the first time everything he's built gets tested against a true 147-pound puncher with title-fight speed.

Garcia and Benn get their next chance to say all this to each other's faces Thursday at T-Mobile Arena.

articles.title: 49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling's Achilles is intact, to undergo MRI on ankle
articles.summary: The way 49ers wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suddenly ended his route and started limping on one leg had everyone thinking the worst.
articles.body:
The way 49ers wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suddenly ended his route and started limping on one leg had everyone thinking the worst.

Stribling has an injured left ankle, coach Kyle Shanahan said after the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams, but the rookie's Achilles is intact.

Stribling will undergo further medical testing to determine the severity of the injury.

He injured his ankle early in the game and was questionable to return, but after running up and down the sideline, Stribling did return.

With 7:16 remaining in the first half, though, Stribling pulled up while running a route. He could not put any weight on his left leg and needed help to get to the sideline medical tent. Eventually, Stribling was carted to the X-ray room.

articles.title: Keys to the game: How do the Bengals beat the Bucs?
articles.summary: Breaking down what the Bengals must do to beat Tampa Bay and start the season 1-0.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals are getting ready to host Tampa Bay on Sept. 13 as the regular season gets underway at Paycor Stadium.

Tampa and Cincinnati enter the season with high expectations. Both teams underachieved in 2025, winning a combined 14 games. The Buccaneers and Bengals are popular picks to win their respective divisions and haven't played each other since 2022, making for an intriguing Week 1 matchup.

Here's what the Bengals must do to beat the Bucs and start the season with a win.

Score early and don't allow Bucs' pass rush to get rolling

Tampa Bay's head coach, Todd Bowles, is known for the different pressure packages he uses in a game.

Bowles has the respect of the Bengals' coaching staff and players.

"Todd has been doing it for a long time," head coach Zac Taylor said of the Bucs' coach. "Todd's got a lot of respect for the pressure they put on you. He's got the pieces he likes. Makes it challenging for an offense."

Yaya Diaby , Vita Vea and rookie Reuben Bain are three players who are most likely to cause issues for Cincinnati's offensive line. Diaby led the Bucs with seven sacks last season. Vea is regarded as one of the top interior defensive linemen in the NFL, with 4.5 sacks and seven tackles for loss in 2025. Vea signed a one-year extension with the Tampa ahead of the season after requesting a trade.

The Bengals will need to get the ball out of quarterback Joe Burrow 's hands quickly, and if Cincinnati can get up on Tampa early, it will negate the Bucs' ability to gain momentum with their pass rushers.

Contain Bucs' standout wide receiver Emeka Egbuka

Veteran quarterback Baker Mayfield is capable of taking over a game when he's in rhythm with former Ohio State standout wide receiver Emeka Egbuka.

In his rookie season, Egbuka proved he's an elite talent in the NFL catching 63 passes for 938 yards and six touchdowns.

Bengals cornerback DJ Turner is likely to draw the assignment of keeping Egbuka in check for most of the game alongside Dax Hill. Turner's status will be closely monitored through Sunday after appearing on the injury report on Sept.10 with a hamstring injury.

Cincinnati's front office didn't give Turner a contract extension ahead of the season for a reason. If Turner can keep a player like Egbuka to limited production, it will help his case in wanting to be paid long-term by the Bengals.

Tackle well and keep Tampa's running back duo to under 100 rushing yards

Despite a down year in the NFC South, one of the bright spots for the Bucs was the play of their running backs. Bucky Irving and Rachaad White combined for 1,160 yards on 305 carries for five touchdowns.

The Bengals struggled to tackle at a high level in 2025, and in order to get to where they want to be in late January, they must be better in this area.

If they can prevent the Bucs' running backs from big runs with sound tackling, it could force Tampa to throw the ball more. The Bengals invested in their defensive line heavily this offseason to create more opportunities to rush the passer.

Sunday's game against Tampa will be the first time the Bengals' new-look defensive line will take the field together for a regular season game.

Aug 6, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (2) participates in training camp at AdventHealth Training Center. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images

Week 3: Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Rachaad White (1) runs with the ball as New York Jets cornerback Sauce Gardner attempts to make the tackle during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. The Buccaneers wore their famous "Creamsicle" throwback uniforms in the 29-27 win.

articles.title: White Sox Minor League Update: September 10, 2026
articles.summary: Pitching sinks Charlotte, while a quiet offense dooms Birmingham
articles.body:
Buffalo Bison 11, Charlotte Knights 4 The Charlotte Knights stumbled to an 11-4 loss to the Buffalo Bisons in a game that remained competitive for five innings before spiraling wildly out of control.

Adisyn Coffey took the mound as an opener for Charlotte, making just his third start of the season. It quickly became the Lenyn Sosa revenge game. The former White Sox infielder greeted Coffey with a leadoff solo shot in the top of the third. Coffey retired the next two hitters, but a single and an RBI double followed, giving Buffalo a 2-0 edge.

The Knights answered in the bottom half of the inning. Rikuu Nishida drew a two-out walk, and Riley Unroe brought him home with a triple to trim the deficit to one.

After Peyton Pallette got the final out of the third inning, Huascar Brazobán followed Coffey and turned in a successful inning of rehab work, surrendering only one hit in a scoreless fourth. Tanner McDougal took over in the fifth and faced the minimum, setting the stage for Charlotte to pull even in the bottom half when Junior Perez launched a solo shot to knot the score at 2-2.

Unfortunately, that was as good as the night would get for the Knights.

After cruising through the fifth, McDougal got into a heap of trouble in the sixth. A walk, a single, an RBI double by Sosa and another base hit pushed the Bisons ahead, 5-2. With one out and the sacks packed, Jairo Iriarte entered to try to limit the damage.

Iriarte surrendered a run-scoring single that made it 6-2, although he recovered to strike out the next two batters and finally end the mess.

Buffalo put the game well out of reach in the seventh, scoring four unearned runs to stretch its advantage to 10-2. Apparently deciding an eight-run lead was not quite enough, the Bisons tacked on another tally when Chad Pinder put in shortstop Jason Matthews in the eighth for fun. Matthews also pitched the ninth and, despite hitting a batter and surrendering a double, he didn't give up a run.

The Knights managed to push across two runs in the bottom of the eighth with the assistance of four walks and a ground out, but the game was way over by then. Charlotte could not generate anything further, settling for an ugly 11-4 defeat.

MVP Junior Perez: 1-for-4, R, RBI, HR, 2 K

Runners-Up Riley Unroe:1-for-2, RBI, 2 BB, 3B Tim Elko : 1-for-3, 2B, BB, K Huascar Brazobán: 1 IP, 1 H, 0 BB, 0 K

Cold Cat Tanner McDougal: 1 1/3 IP, 4 H, 4 R, 2 BB, K, L

Runners-Up Adisyn Coffey: 2 2/3 IP, 3 H, 2 R, 0 BB, K Jake Cave : 0-for-4, 4 K

Knoxville Smokies 4, Birmingham Barons 1 The Barons' offense remained silent for most of the night, and a late rally fell well short in a loss to the Smokies.

Juan Carela matched Knoxville zero for zero through the first four innings as the game developed into an old-fashioned pitchers' duel. The Smokies finally broke the stalemate in the fifth, using a single, a ground out and another single to grab a 1-0 lead.

That was the only damage against Carela. The righthander delivered five strong innings, allowing one run on three hits with one walk and five strikeouts.

Birmingham had its best opportunity to answer in the bottom of the fifth. Calvin Harris opened the frame with a one-out single, but Jacob Burke followed by grounding into a force out that erased Harris at second. Dylan Campbell then delivered the Barons' only extra-base hit of the night, a double that moved Burke to third, and Caleb Bonemer worked a four-pitch walk to load the bases.

Unfortunately, Alec Briley grounded out, and Birmingham came away empty-handed.

Jackson Kelley took over in the sixth and retired the side in order, but things unraveled during his next inning of work. The Smokies tagged him for two runs on four hits and a walk, stretching their advantage to 3-0.

Garrett Wright surrendered another tally in the ninth, leaving the Barons staring at a four-run deficit and three final outs to do something about it.

Ryan Burrowes and Samuel Zavala opened the bottom of the ninth with back-to-back walks, but José Colmenares struck out, and Harris flew out, leaving Birmingham down to its final out. Burke finally broke up the shutout with an RBI single, and Campbell worked a walk to keep the line moving. Bonemer couldn't produce a miracle, though, grounding out to end the game.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia's road to redemption continues against Conor Benn on Mexican Independence Day weekend
articles.summary: While Garcia proved to the world that he was back in business with his title-reclaiming victory over Mario Barrios in April, a victory over Conor Benn on Mex...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS – It's no secret that Ryan Garcia is among the most polarizing and talked about athletes in North America, though that conversation has often veered sideways in recent couple years. While Garcia proved to the world that he was back in business with his title-reclaiming victory over Mario Barrios in April, a victory over Conor Benn on Mexican Independence Day weekend would truly solidify his return to the top of the sport.

After Garcia's 2024 win against Devin Haney was overturned due to a failed drug test, the now 28-year-old Victorville, CA native had a several month stretch in the limelight that could only be described as destructive. He had fallen into an intense and violent drinking habit which seemed to take place entirely on camera, and a series of racist remarks made on a livestream July 2024 resulted in a lengthy expulsion from the WBC.

Few athletes in the modern era, if any, have experienced the highs and lows of the social media zeitgeist than Garcia has. A major reason for his transcendent popularity is the fact that he's as much of a famous internet personality as he is a champion boxer, essentially the reverse of Jake Paul-ification of the sport. While many internet celebrities have used their personalities as a way to get into prize fighting, Garica used his notoriety as a fighter to boost his popularity as an influencer.

"You know, I have a vision," Garcia said. "I understand that there's a new way of promoting yourself. There's a new way of media. I don't let what anybody says really get to me as long as I'm preparing well and I'm sharp. I don't really care what they say. They've been saying that since I was doing Instagram back in the day. 'He's an Instagram fighter'. Now I'm a streamer, so it's the same thing, just a different lingo. I'm not really too concerned about people's opinions."

For all intents and purposes, Garcia has seemed much healthier in all regards since making his return to the ring in May 2025 after a year-long hiatus. He was upset by Rolly Romero that night at the Fatal Fury event in Times Square, but responded with that dominant unanimous decision win over Barrios this past April. Entering Saturday's bout, Garcia is looking to earn consecutive (official) wins for the first time since 2022.

While Garcia certainly could have made more of a statement against Barrios, the fact he proved he could still dominate a title fight was enough to write home about. Saturday is different. If Garcia can finish a much more respected fighter in Benn and do so in the way many expect him to, he'd essentially be in a position to make any championship bout he wants. From the sounds of Garcia's comments at Thursday's press conference, it appears he'll be at 147 for a little while with his eyes set on a rematch against Devin Haney.

"I don't really like to think too far ahead," Garcia said. "I'm very comfortable at 147. This is the most prestigious weight class other than heavyweight, so I'm going to be here for a long time. Hopefully I get to kick Devin Haney's ass again."

And given the significance of the fight's date and what it means to Garcia as a Mexican-American, that's enough of a reason to expect the best Garcia we've seen to date. Doubly so considering that Benn has used Garcia's American birthplace as a way to minimize his Mexican roots.

"As long as I'm sharp and beating the sh*t out of him, it's a great performance," Garcia said. "Do I want to beat him so bad and make a statement where he's not even close? Yes. And finish the job? One hundred percent. I'm not looking to fight on this date and not give the fans a spectacular night. I'm here to give the fans everything they wanted and more."

articles.title: Yankees news: Anthony Volpe gets brutally honest on 'whirlwind' of getting back to majors
articles.summary: Anthony Volpe did not have a quiet return to the big leagues. He made it as loud as he could, and he did it with his bat during Thursday’s series finale aga...
articles.body:
Anthony Volpe did not have a quiet return to the big leagues . He made it as loud as he could, and he did it with his bat during Thursday's series finale against the Colorado Rockies at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx.

In his first game back to the majors, Volpe went 3-for-5 with five RBIs. His grand slam in the seventh inning further buried the Rockies, as it stretched New York's lead to eight runs, 10-2. The Yankees ultimately won the game to the tune of a 10-3 score.

"Unexpected whirlwind," the 25-year-old Volpe said following the game, describing what the past 24 hours had been for him (h/t Gary Phillips of NY Daily News Sports).

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Volpe was sent to the minors in August amid his struggles. George Lombard Jr. was then called up by the Yankees , taking over Volpe's shortstop role in the majors. Now, Volpe is back with the show, but as a second baseman, with Jazz Chisholm Jr. , hitting the injured list.

Those who have continued to follow Volpe even after he was sent to the minors may not be so surprised to see him shine in his first game back to the big leagues. After his demotion, he hit .284 (31-for-109) with 10 home runs and a 1.023 OPS .

Volpe's future as a second baseman with the Yankees remains uncertain, but he clearly grabbed attention with his performance against the Rockies. If anything, he might have fans' hope in him up again, and it's on him to sustain his form and capitalize on the new opportunity to contribute to New York.

Before his demotion, Volpe was hitting .240/.325/.322 with just a home run and 19 RBIs in 56 games.

articles.title: Head coach Pete Furey gets first win as Niskayuna routs Colonie in Section 2 football
articles.summary: Niskayuna had scoring plays from all three phases and Pete Furey celebrated his first victory on Thursday night with a dominating 51-18 win over Colonie.
articles.body:
NISKAYUNA - The Pete Furey era has been ignited at Niskayuna.

Furey, in his first season as head football coach at his alma mater, celebrated his first victory Thursday night with a dominating 51-18 win over Colonie.

Niskayuna (1-1) had scoring plays from all three phases - offense, defense and special teams - in finding the end zone eight times against the Wolf Pack (1-1).

"There's a lot of emotions," said Furey, the former defensive coordinator who replaced retiring Brian Grastorf over the summer. "Man, there's a lot of emotions. I've won a lot on this field, and I won as a coach a lot, but not as a head coach. I don't want to take the credit. These guys work their butts off. These guys earned it. It's their win, it's not mine."

In a critical game for Class AA playoff positioning, Niskayuna bounced back from last week's 41-20 loss to Shaker, rolling up 340 yards of offense and limiting Colonie to 191.

Furey is a 2009 graduate of Niskayuna, where he played for his father, John, who was head coach for 22 years. John Furey is one of his son's assistants on the current Niskayuna staff.

"We're so happy for him," senior linebacker David Sullivan said of his coach. "First of many. We're very proud of him. He's doing a great job. He's a great guy, but even better, coach."

The game seemed destined to be a back-and-forth affair when Colonie, on a 60-yard pass from Steven Thomas Jr. to Kaiden Hill, made it 13-12 just before the first quarter ended.

Niskayuna needed just two plays to answer, going 60 yards and scoring 11 seconds into the second quarter on Chase Meisner's 23-yard run. Nisky ran away from Colonie after that.

"I brought them together on the sideline," Furey said. "I told them they had to make a decision. Are they going to show up tonight? Are they not going to show up? After we got made a few big plays, they decided they were going to show up, and we showed up."

Quarterback Thomas Boler completed 9 of 16 passes for 156 yards and two touchdowns.

"Boler's been unbelievable," Furey said. "The way he sees the defense, the way he can put the ball on the money, on time.

"He's just different. Man, he's earned it. He's worked for it. He put the work in, so it's paying off now."

Boler gave Niskayuna the lead for good on a 32-yard touchdown pass to Joey DiPiazza. He later connected with Poem Staten in the end zone for 42 yards.

38: Consecutive points scored by Niskayuna from the start of the second quarter until midway through the final period.

11: Niskayuna players who touched the ball on offense, either rushing or receiving or both.

3: Return touchdowns for Niskayuna - one on a kickoff (80 yards by DiPiazza), one on an interception (36 yards by Staten) and one on a punt (41 yards by Meisner).

Colonie: The Wolf Pack return home to face Schenectady at 7 p.m. on Friday.

Niskayuna: Next on the schedule is a trip to Schenectady at 7 p.m. on Friday.

articles.title: Kaelon Black surprisingly involved in NFL debut
articles.summary: Rookie Kaelon Black had 14 carries, four more than Christian McCaffrey, for 65 yards in a solid Week 1 showing versus LA.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers RB Kaelon Black had a game-high 14 carries for 65 yards against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1. He added a five-yard reception on his lone target.

Why It Matters: For years, the 49ers have steadfastly refused to utilize a second running back in any meaningful way when Christian McCaffrey has been available. On Thursday, they did just that, giving the rookie 14 rushing attempts -- that was four more than McCaffrey, and five more than last year's RB2 Brian Robinson had in any game. Black delivered, too, running hard and posting a healthy 4.6 yards per carry. You never want to read too much into Week 1, and there were extenuating circumstances with the game taking place in Australia, but Black did enough to warrant adding off waivers if he's out there.
